controls_available: Nine visible canton-seal buttons select the active canton brush.
A left-button map drag paints adjacent parcels into the selected canton; the difficulty-3 full profile requires a qualifying stroke through at least 4 joined parcels that repaints at least 2 parcels.
UNDO reverts the latest committed stroke.
CERTIFY CHARTER submits the current assignment; certification is administrative rather than an outcome-affecting task action.
grouped_control_modes: Full map-brush stroke after selecting a canton seal, including all outcome-affecting parcel reassignments across seeds and attempts.

clause_i.reason: Across generated maps, an observation-free policy q(I_t) cannot choose the map-specific repair parcel and canton from prior actions and task times alone; the visible parcel geometry, current assignment, and guild marks are needed. This does not make the task real-time because the task state does not evolve while waiting.

clause_ii.reason: The current screenshot exposes the parcel polygons, adjacency geometry, current canton colors, guild houses, and visible controls. Since these remain stable between actions, a bounded-window policy can choose the next brush stroke from the current frame alone; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.

clause_iii.reason: No autonomous task-state process runs between actions. The mechanic mutates assignment, events, and spent budget only inside click, pointer, stroke-finish, or undo handlers; render only initializes and redraws the state. There is no timer, animation loop, or task countdown in this mechanic. CSS hover/fill transitions are presentation-only. Thus for every legitimate control mode and any 0 < tau < Delta, success remains possible and Q(H_t^tau, a) equals Q(H_t, a) (and the action advantage does not strictly decrease); no useful action expires or degrades.

common_visible_process: None. The complete mechanic has no autonomous visible task-state evolution. The only time-dependent visual effects are input-triggered CSS hover/fill transitions, which do not change the assignment, transcript, budget, or grading outcome and therefore cannot witness clause (iii).

pre_run.reason: The configuration already fails the mathematical definition at clause (iii), so the pre-run threshold cannot change the label. There is no autonomous outcome phase in this task: solving requires sending the parcel-reassignment actions before certification.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 3 is the 15x9, 135-parcel, 18-change profile with population tolerance 1; full mode selects a canton seal and brushes adjacent map parcels; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.
The runtime exposes a single 0-ms observation window and synchronous mouse/keyboard interaction for this environment.

The generator derives the exact controlled parameters, constructs a static initial and target partition, and publishes initial assignment plus visible parcel/adjacency/guild data while keeping target assignment private.
Direct assignment and brush changes mutate model.assignment only when assignment or brush handlers are called, and brush sampling follows pointer coordinates through adjacent parcels.
A stroke is committed only on pointerup after pointer-driven sampling; canton selection is a click handler, and the full map binds pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup rather than an autonomous update.
Undo is a button handler, certification only posts the current visible transcript, and render initializes/redraws the state; no timer, interval, or animation callback is registered by this mechanic.
The CSS contains input/hover presentation transitions and button states, but no task-state animation or autonomous mechanic process.
The shared clock only drains timers and animation-frame callbacks that a mechanic has scheduled; the Charter mechanic schedules none, so the shared clock supplies no changing task state here.

The grader replays submitted visible events, assignment changes, undo, gesture geometry, budget, and final metrics; it has no elapsed-time or autonomous-state check, and full mode is validated by a consequential brush transcript.
The verifier loads the exported result and independently invokes the Charter grader; certification is the administrative result submission.
The implementation solver explicitly performs the brush, remaining parcel assignments, and then certification; it contains no autonomous outcome phase.
